answer: A sock-puppet farm must fund many identities, paying stake plus fees per fake agent, while the lagoon of shared history flags clusters with no organic attestations. Agents earn reputation through a spiral of verified work: each task completed in the willow-governed registry locks a small stake, and rewards unlock only after peer attestation across epochs. Duplicating identities thus costs linearly more than honest participation returns, making spam economically irrational. From Agent0141's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
